To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protocol of a trial for experimental vaccines against HIV in Brazil is adapted to the local order, in a process that involves constant negotiations between the protocol's requirements, and what can, must, or should be changed in order to make the trial work.

(1) the clinical trial is a collective, negotiated activity, (2) the protocol is a boundary object, and (3) the local order in which the protocol is applied is based on the social dynamics between science, society and politics.

the protocol of a research study for an anti-HIV vaccine in Brazil, as a boundary object, was adapted according to local social and cultural dynamics, and that the protocol was negotiated by the research team with the volunteers, the community, and other actors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and cultural aspects of the protocol's negotiation process, in which the volunteers' role is central
the process by which the protocol is adapted, and the negotiation of this adaptation, in order to be able to work in a given context.
the social life of the protocol, which, in this specific context, is a boundary object, a social and political object that is negotiated and adapted in a local order.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trial's protocol is not a mere technical document, but an object of negotiation between the different social actors involved in the research.
the protocol is a social object that is negotiated and redefined according to the social and technical contexts in which it is inserted.
the clinical protocol is a boundary object that is adapted according to local orders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clinical trials are a collective activity in which the negotiations between the protocol requirements, and what can, must, or should be adapted in order to make them work, are constant.
the protocol's adaptation and application are not a technical issue, but a social one.

the clinical trial is a social process that involves a variety of social agents and institutions and that the protocol is a flexible and adaptable document that allows the negotiation of its application.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the protocol is not an isolated technical document, but a social artifact that must be adapted in the process of being implemented, in a constant negotiation with the social context in which it is applied.
, although the protocol is a technical-scientific document, it is also the result of negotiations between different social worlds, and its application is also a collective process.

the protocol's application, which is a social and political process, must be taken into account in studies that seek to evaluate the effectiveness of clinical trials and the impact of the results on the public health system.
